title: Impact of Minimum Drinking Age on Alcohol Consumption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
This is a Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) analysis. The legal drinking age of 21 creates a sharp discontinuity where treatment assignment (legal drinking status) changes deterministically at the cutoff. The key assumption is that individuals just below and just above age 21 are comparable in all characteristics except their legal drinking status, allowing us to identify the causal effect of reaching the legal drinking age on alcohol consumption.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s95_data.csv")

# Convert running_var to represent distance from age 21 cutoff
# Assuming running_var is already centered at the cutoff (0 = age 21)
data$age_from_21 <- data$running_var

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$age_from_21, c = 0)

# Print main results
cat("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Coefficient (Treatment Effect):", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(rdd_result$z[1], 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ",", round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]\n")
cat("Bandwidth:", round(rdd_result$bws[1,1], 4), "\n")
cat("Number of observations:", rdd_result$N[1], "\n")

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Different bandwidths
bw_half <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$age_from_21, c = 0, h = rdd_result$bws[1,1] * 0.5)
bw_double <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$age_from_21, c = 0, h = rdd_result$bws[1,1] * 2)

cat("Half bandwidth (", round(bw_half$bws[1,1], 4), "):", round(bw_half$coef[1], 4), 
    " (SE:", round(bw_half$se[1], 4), ")\n")
cat("Double bandwidth (", round(bw_double$bws[1,1], 4), "):", round(bw_double$coef[1], 4), 
    " (SE:", round(bw_double$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 2. Different polynomial orders
rdd_quad <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$age_from_21, c = 0, p = 2)
cat("Quadratic polynomial:", round(rdd_quad$coef[1], 4), 
    " (SE:", round(rdd_quad$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 3. Bias-corrected results
cat("Bias-corrected estimate:", round(rdd_result$coef[2], 4), 
    " (SE:", round(rdd_result$se[2], 4), ")\n")

# Manipulation test
manipulation_test <- rddensity(data$age_from_21, c = 0)
cat("\nManipulation Test (McCrary density test):\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(manipulation_test$test$t_jk, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(manipulation_test$test$p_jk, 4), "\n")

# Summary statistics around cutoff
cat("\n=== DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS ===\n")
left_side <- data[data$age_from_21 < 0 & data$age_from_21 >= -rdd_result$bws[1,1], ]
right_side <- data[data$age_from_21 >= 0 & data$age_from_21 <= rdd_result$bws[1,1], ]

cat("Mean outcome below cutoff:", round(mean(left_side$y, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
cat("Mean outcome above cutoff:", round(mean(right_side$y, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
cat("Difference in means:", round(mean(right_side$y, na.rm = TRUE) - mean(left_side$y, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")

# Visualization
rdplot(y = data$y, x = data$age_from_21, c = 0, 
       title = "RDD: Effect of Legal Drinking Age on Alcohol Consumption",
       x.label = "Age relative to 21st birthday (months)",
       y.label = "Alcohol Consumption")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive and significant coefficient of approximately 0.3-0.6, indicating that reaching the legal drinking age of 21 increases alcohol consumption. This is based on economic theory suggesting that legal access reduces the costs (both monetary and risk-related) of obtaining alcohol. The effect should be immediate and discrete at the cutoff, as individuals gain legal access to purchase alcohol in bars, restaurants, and stores. Previous empirical studies on this topic typically find significant increases in alcohol consumption when individuals reach the legal drinking age, though the magnitude varies depending on the measurement of consumption and the specific population studied.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The identification strategy leverages the age-21 drinking age cutoff as a natural experiment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Reaching the age of 21 leads to an increase in alcohol consumption.
